title: Student Federation v. University of Delhi
text: The petitioner, a student federation, filed a writ petition under Article 226 challenging the university's decision to increase examination fees by 300% without following any transparent procedure. The petition alleged violation of the fundamental right to education as a component of the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. The High Court issued a writ of mandamus to the university to disclose the basis for the fee hike and to hold consultations with student representatives. The arbitrary increase in fees without due process violates the principles of natural justice and the fundamental rights of students. The High Court directs the university to constitute a Fee Revision Committee and to maintain fee levels until the committee reports. This order exercises the High Court's power under Article 226 to enforce fundamental rights against institutions performing public functions.
